svg.aria-label: SATLIB parity-learning A*s = b (mod 2) inner-product system compiled via binary Tseitin XOR trees

g.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
g.text: SATLIB Parity-Learning Benchmarks: par8 / par16 / par32 (satlib-dimacs-parity)
Crawford–Kearns–Schapire (1994) learning parity over k ∈ {8, 16, 32} bits: A · s = b (mod 2) compiled via binary Tseitin XOR trees
1. Parity-Learning Linear System: A · s = b (mod 2)
Recover unknown secret parity mask s ∈ 𝔽₂ᵏ from labeled sample vectors a⁽ⁱ⁾
Row 3: a⁽³⁾ · s = s₁ ⊕ s₃ ⊕ s₅ ⊕ s₇ = b₃ (mod 2)
Each active parity row is compiled into a binary Tseitin XOR tree;
all 30 instances are planted SAT (5 random seeds × k ∈ {8, 16, 32} × {orig, -c}).
2. Binary Tseitin XOR Tree Decomposition (CNF ↔ XCNF)
3. Scaling Across par8 / par16 / par32 (orig vs. -c)
Only CryptoMiniSat (30/30, 11.2 s) solves all par32 via native XOR Gaussian elimination.
